observations:
Torah LM2/49 is a short six-paragraph teaching focused on the themes of teshuvah, divine mercy, and redirecting the passion of the yetzer hara into holy service. The entire Torah operates primarily on the eitza (cause-and-effect) axis. A thorough search for any independent domain of 3+ bechina-connected concepts yields the following:

1. TESHUVAH CLUSTER: The Torah centers on teshuvah (repentance). The Rebbe defines true teshuvah as returning through the same places of temptation and turning away. He uses 'נִקְרָא' (is called), a bechina marker, to identify that action AS teshuvah. However, only two nodes are involved (the action and תְּשׁוּבָה). No third bechina-linked node in the source text completes a cluster of 3+. The mercy of God (רַחֲמִים) appears as a premise for why teshuvah is accessible, but it is not given a bechina equation with teshuvah — it is the causal context (because God is merciful, teshuvah is possible). Insufficient for a new package.

2. THOUGHT-DEED CLUSTER: The Rebbe states that thought (מַחֲשָׁבָה) IS deed (עֲשִׂיָּה) for people in this spiritual situation, using the identity verb 'הִיא'. This is a genuine bechina pair. However, only two nodes are identified with this equivalence. No third concept is explicitly given bechina identity with either thought or deed in this Torah. The text says 'גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הָעֲשִׂיָּה יֵשׁ מַחֲשָׁבָה' (even in the world of asiyah there is thought), but this is an elaboration of the same identity statement, not a third bechina node. Insufficient for a new package.

3. YETZER HARA — PASSION — PRAYER CLUSTER: The Rebbe teaches that the warmth and passion (חֲמִימוּת, הִתְלַהֲבוּת) of the yetzer hara can be redirected into prayer and service. This is a pure eitza: the passion PRODUCES fervent prayer when redirected. The Rebbe does not say that the yetzer hara's passion IS the same essential thing as holy fervor; rather, the physical energy of passion is channeled (eitza) into prayer. No bechina identifications are made in this cluster.

4. EVIL MIRROR: The Torah does not develop an evil counterpart package. The yetzer hara is present as the source of passion to be redirected, but it is not given bechina equations with other evil concepts. The teaching's thrust is entirely about turning the negative force toward holiness, not about mapping evil structures.

CONCLUSION: With only two bechina pairs found in the source text (both pairs of 2 nodes, not 3+), and with zero bechina edges in the dataset, no new packages can be formed for LM2/49. The Torah is structured as a practical teaching (machzor mussar) about the accessibility of teshuvah and the value of the yetzer hara, communicated through a tightly compressed eitza chain with embedded bechina identifications too thin to sustain independent packages. If the two bechina pairs flagged in torah_49_additions.json were added to the dataset as bechina edges, they would each form a 2-node isolated component — still below the threshold for independent packages.
